read.where: **Brandy** is distilled from **wine** (or other fermented fruit). In the EU, brandy ages at least **one year** in large oak, or **six months** in casks under 1,000 liters. Fruit brandies are named for their fruit: apple brandy, pear brandy and more.

read.bigIdea: Twice distilled, from one region of France.
read.where: **Cognac** comes from the Cognac region of France, mostly from **Ugni Blanc** grapes. It is distilled **twice** in **copper pot stills** and aged in **French oak**. The grade tells the age of the youngest brandy: **VS** at least **2 years**, **VSOP** at least **4**, **XO** at least **10** (since 2018).

keyPoints.line: is one of them; nothing to do with sparkling wine.

read.bigIdea: Six growing areas, named on the label.
read.where: Cognac’s vineyards are split into **crus**: **Grande Champagne**, **Petite Champagne**, **Borderies**, **Fins Bois**, **Bons Bois** and **Bois Ordinaires**. **Fine Champagne** on a label means a blend of Grande and Petite Champagne. Here “Champagne” is a place name: it has nothing to do with the sparkling wine.

read.bigIdea: Three more brandies guests ask for.
read.where: **Armagnac** is grape brandy from **Gascony** in southwest France. **Calvados** is **apple** brandy (pears allowed) from **Normandy**. **Pisco** is grape brandy from **Peru** and **Chile**. Peruvian styles: **puro** (one grape), **aromático** (aromatic grapes), **acholado** (a blend of grapes) and **mosto verde** (distilled before fermentation finishes, so it’s rounder).

keyPoints.line: is Cognac, lemon and orange liqueur.
has egg white for a foamy top.
is rye, Cognac, vermouth and Bénédictine.

read.bigIdea: The Sidecar, Pisco Sour and Vieux Carré.
read.where: The **Sidecar** is Cognac, lemon and orange liqueur. The **Pisco Sour** is pisco, lime, sugar and egg white. The **Brandy Alexander** is Cognac, crème de cacao and cream. The **Vieux Carré** is rye, Cognac, sweet vermouth and Bénédictine.

facts.fact: Brandy is distilled from wine (or other fermented fruit). In the EU, brandy ages at least one year in large oak, or six months in casks under 1,000 liters. Fruit brandies are named for their fruit: apple brandy, pear brandy and more.

facts.fact: Cognac comes from the Cognac region of France, mostly from Ugni Blanc grapes. It is distilled twice in copper pot stills and aged in French oak. The grade tells the age of the youngest brandy: VS at least 2 years, VSOP at least 4, XO at least 10 (since 2018).

facts.fact: Armagnac is grape brandy from Gascony in southwest France. Calvados is apple brandy (pears allowed) from Normandy. Pisco is grape brandy from Peru and Chile. Peruvian styles: puro (one grape), aromático (aromatic grapes), acholado (a blend of grapes) and mosto verde (distilled before fermentation finishes, so it’s rounder).

The Sidecar is Cognac, lemon and orange liqueur. The Pisco Sour is pisco, lime, sugar and egg white. The Brandy Alexander is Cognac, crème de cacao and cream. The Vieux Carré is rye, Cognac, sweet vermouth and Bénédictine.
